**Analysis of the test image:**

- **Affected part**: Tomato leaf (based on leaf shape and size)
- **Key features**:
  - Large, irregular brown-tan necrotic area covering much of the leaf, most prominent toward the leaf margin and tip
  - Significant yellowing (chlorosis) surrounding the necrotic tissue
  - Darker brown/almost black coloration in the center of the necrotic zone
  - The necrotic area appears widest at the leaf margin, tapering inward — a V-like or wedge pattern
  - No visible white fuzzy sporulation (rules out Late Blight)
  - No small discrete spots or halos (rules out Septoria, Bacterial Speck)
  - No powdery white coating (rules out Powdery Mildew)
  - No concentric rings (rules out Early Blight)
  - No gray mold sporulation (rules out Gray Mold)

**Reasoning**: The large wedge/V-shaped necrotic lesion widest at the leaf margin with surrounding irregular yellowing matches Verticillium Wilt most closely. The description specifically notes "V-shaped leaf lesions widest at the leaf margin, brown necrotic tissue surrounded by irregular yellowing." The lesion morphology and color distribution are consistent.
